prompt:
Add a `tasklist` extension: a list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space becomes a task.
- The marker is replaced by `<input type="checkbox">`, `checked` for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` unless the `clickable` option is true (default false).
- The `<li>` gets the class from the `item_class` option (default `task`).
- It works in ordered and unordered lists, nested lists and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker.
Register it so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works once installed.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
Added the `tasklist` extension, and `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` loads it by short name; the full test suite passes, including 17 new tests. flake8 and the docs spellchecker are not installed here, so neither was run.

Behaviours you might not assume:
- **Attribute form:** in the default `xhtml` output the checkbox renders as `<input disabled="disabled" type="checkbox" />`; with `output_format='html'` it is `<input disabled type="checkbox">`.
- **Marker beats reference link:** `- [x] text` becomes a task even if a `[x]: url` reference is defined.
- **Empty items:** `- [x]` with nothing after it is left alone, because the marker must be followed by a space.
- **Empty `item_class`:** setting it to `''` adds no class.

`docs/extensions/index.md` still says no new extensions will be added to the project; I left that note as it is, so it now contradicts this addition.

I also added `checkbox` and `checkboxes` to `.spell-dict` as a precaution.
